content.comment_body: Hello, [product_name] experts. I have worked with [product_name] for three years, mostly handling small automation projects like bowl feeder controls. Recently, I started using the new [article_no] version of [product_name] for a reagent bottle filling system, which involves a solenoid valve, a flowmeter generating 1000 pulses per litre, a reset switch, a foot pedal to start, and two status lights—green for ready, red flashing during filling, and steady red at the end. Everything functions well, but now I need to transfer the liquid volume and elapsed time per container to a central PC for label printing, and I’m unsure how to achieve this. The datalogger feature isn’t suitable for real-time transfer, even though it is simple to use. Could anyone advise how to achieve real-time data transfer? I also looked at the 'Variable Mapping' section in the Help but couldn’t understand its purpose. Thanks in advance for your suggestions.

Hi, For your requirement, an OPC server is necessary. For the [product_name] model you mentioned, I am aware that [product_name] PC Access can be used, with some limitations. Net OPC Server and Libnodave OPC Server are also possible options. An OPC server allows fast data retrieval from the controller to a PC. If you’re familiar with it, you can develop your OPC client, which could be a SCADA system running on a PC. Note that I’m not a specialist. [product_name] PC Access also provides an Excel add-in so you can get data directly into an Excel worksheet. Hope this helps.

Hello, One option is [product_name]Monitor ([url]). This software now exports actual real-time values from [product_name] to Excel. The data you need can easily be selected in the program and is updated in real time.

analysis.insight_summary: The user appreciates the automation abilities of their [product_name] device but needs guidance on exporting real-time data (liquid volume and elapsed time) to a central PC for label creation, as built-in logging does not offer real-time transfer. The 'Variable Mapping' feature is unclear to the user, and they are unsure how to proceed. Other contributors suggest using various OPC servers or external programs that support real-time data transfer to Excel, highlighting a demand for more user-friendly, integrated export solutions.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to transfer real-time operational data from their [product_name] device directly to a central PC in a format suitable for label printing, ideally using a straightforward and efficient method.
